blocks.text: Dohra:

Guru's blessings received gratuitously (are difficult to contain), As people with a serious and profound disposition alone can preserve. It is as if the milk of a lioness can not be preserved, In a bowl of any base metal except that of (pure) gold. (1)
lines: Guru's blessings received gratuitously (are difficult to contain),
As people with a serious and profound disposition alone can preserve.
It is as if the milk of a lioness can not be preserved,
In a bowl of any base metal except that of (pure) gold.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Guru, having awarded the custody of a congregation (to the Hindal Jat), Fixed its jurisdiction over a radius of twenty to thirty villages. Directing him to ask the devout to bow down before him as they did before the Guru, The Guru asked him to continue to visit the Guru as before. (2)
lines: The Guru, having awarded the custody of a congregation (to the Hindal Jat),
Fixed its jurisdiction over a radius of twenty to thirty villages.
Directing him to ask the devout to bow down before him as they did before the Guru,
The Guru asked him to continue to visit the Guru as before.

blocks.text: Warning him against the temptation of declaring himself a Guru, Lest he should be ostracized from the Sikh Panth.
Directing him to make the congregation meditate upon Waheguru's Name, Satguru (Guru Amar Das) gave him instructions to this effect. (3)
lines: Directing him to make the congregation meditate upon Waheguru's Name,
Satguru (Guru Amar Das) gave him instructions to this effect.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Being worthless to appreciate the worth of Guru's gratuitous blessing, He could not maintain and preserve the Guru's rare gift. It is as if an ass having covered its body with a lion's skin, Could devour the people's crops by terrorizing the people. (4)
lines: Being worthless to appreciate the worth of Guru's gratuitous blessing,
He could not maintain and preserve the Guru's rare gift.
It is as if an ass having covered its body with a lion's skin,
Could devour the people's crops by terrorizing the people.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Very rare are such people in this human world, Who do not turn arrogant after acquiring wealth. This (worthless) idiot turning arrogant (after being affluent), Chose to ignore the Guru who had endowed him with wealth. (5)
lines: Very rare are such people in this human world,
Who do not turn arrogant after acquiring wealth.
This (worthless) idiot turning arrogant (after being affluent),
Chose to ignore the Guru who had endowed him with wealth.

blocks.text: Claiming that had he harvested the rewards of good deeds of his past, The Guru had no powers to endow him with his present affluence. Having constructed a tank copying the design of Guru's sacred pool, He labeled his cattle pond as the sacred Ganges. (6)
lines: Claiming that had he harvested the rewards of good deeds of his past,
The Guru had no powers to endow him with his present affluence.
Having constructed a tank copying the design of Guru's sacred pool,
He labeled his cattle pond as the sacred Ganges.

blocks.text: Including the cow-slaughterers in his sect after ablutions in the pond, He made himself a rival to the Guru in this way. Moreover, I would narrate how he eclipsed Guru's glory, And how he converted himself into a Niranjania to harm Sikhism. (7)
lines: Including the cow-slaughterers in his sect after ablutions in the pond,
He made himself a rival to the Guru in this way.
Moreover,
I would narrate how he eclipsed Guru's glory,
And how he converted himself into a Niranjania to harm Sikhism.

blocks.text: Guru Nanak is reported as an incarnation of king Janak1 (in Janamsakhi), He interpolated the Janamsakhi2 making Nanak the servant of Janak. Interpolating further, he declared himself the son-in-law of Janak, Thereby making himself the co-brother of Ramachandra3 . (8)
lines: Guru Nanak is reported as an incarnation of king Janak1 (in Janamsakhi),
He interpolated the Janamsakhi2 making Nanak the servant of Janak.
Interpolating further, he declared himself the son-in-law of Janak,
Thereby making himself the co-brother of Ramachandra3 .

blocks.text: Dohra:

Sometime he remarked that there used to be a saint, Whom another devout Sikh had rendered some service. But when the saint wished to bless him, he failed to arrive, And the Hindal Jat got the saint's blessings in his place surreptitiously. (9)
lines: Sometime he remarked that there used to be a saint,
Whom another devout Sikh had rendered some service.
But when the saint wished to bless him, he failed to arrive,
And the Hindal Jat got the saint's blessings in his place surreptitiously.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Sometime claiming himself to be a self-made saint, He denied that the Guru had any powers to bless him. Claiming further that he knew the whole mystery (of creation), He declared that the ignorant masses had a blind faith (in the Guru). (10)
lines: Sometime claiming himself to be a self-made saint,
He denied that the Guru had any powers to bless him.
Claiming further that he knew the whole mystery (of creation),
He declared that the ignorant masses had a blind faith (in the Guru).

blocks.text: Dohra:

Drafting such fictitious claims (about his own powers), He made a number of interpolations in the Janamsakhi. He claimed that even Dhru Prehlad4 could not achieve that spiritual status, Which he (the Hindal) had achieved (with his own efforts). (11)
lines: Drafting such fictitious claims (about his own powers),
He made a number of interpolations in the Janamsakhi.
He claimed that even Dhru Prehlad4 could not achieve that spiritual status,
Which he (the Hindal) had achieved (with his own efforts).

blocks.text: Chaupai:

He fabricated further tales to eclipse the Guru's glory, By declaring that his own Guru was still alive. Above all, crossing all sense of decency and propriety, He declared that Guru Nanak was still alive as 'Jinda Pir'. (12)
lines: He fabricated further tales to eclipse the Guru's glory,
By declaring that his own Guru was still alive.
Above all, crossing all sense of decency and propriety,
He declared that Guru Nanak was still alive as 'Jinda Pir'.

blocks.text: Referring to Alexander's slave named Jinda, He declared the Guru Nanak's spirit resided in him. Declaring himself as the third brother of Guru Nanak and Saint Kabir, He made such an interpolations in the Janamsakhi. (13)
lines: Referring to Alexander's slave named Jinda,
He declared the Guru Nanak's spirit resided in him.
Declaring himself as the third brother of Guru Nanak and Saint Kabir,
He made such an interpolations in the Janamsakhi.

blocks.text: Dohra:

His (blasphemous deeds of making interpolations) cast him, In the image of a rider in a caravan of horse-riders from Delhi. Although he might have joined the caravan midway, And that too riding on an ass among the horse-riders. (14)
lines: His (blasphemous deeds of making interpolations) cast him,
In the image of a rider in a caravan of horse-riders from Delhi.
Although he might have joined the caravan midway,
And that too riding on an ass among the horse-riders.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

If, perchance, somebody enquired about the caravan's (destination), He would respond to enquiries ahead of others. He declared that the five riders (including himself) rode from Delhi, Such was the ingenuity and guile of this ass rider. (15)
lines: If, perchance, somebody enquired about the caravan's (destination),
He would respond to enquiries ahead of others.
He declared that the five riders (including himself) rode from Delhi,
Such was the ingenuity and guile of this ass rider.

blocks.text: Such were the (blasphemous) deeds of this Hindal Jat, That my dear gursikh readers must listen to these. Further, the progeny which sprang up from the loins of this Hindal, Made even more atrocious and shocking insertions. (16)
lines: Such were the (blasphemous) deeds of this Hindal Jat,
That my dear gursikh readers must listen to these.
Further, the progeny which sprang up from the loins of this Hindal,
Made even more atrocious and shocking insertions.

blocks.text: I would narrate all the names of this (notorious) progeny, And the way they met their doom (for their misdeeds). Since they failed to preserve the Guru's blessing acquired gratis, They made many more fictitious interpolations in (Janamsakhis). (17)
lines: I would narrate all the names of this (notorious) progeny,
And the way they met their doom (for their misdeeds).
Since they failed to preserve the Guru's blessing acquired gratis,
They made many more fictitious interpolations in (Janamsakhis).

blocks.text: Dohra:

The sons who were born to this Hindal, (a Jat by caste), Did follow the Sikh tenets and Sikh way of life to some extent. But the grandsons who succeeded the Hindal 's sons, Had gone completely astray from the Sikh way of life. (18)
lines: The sons who were born to this Hindal,
(a Jat by caste),
Did follow the Sikh tenets and Sikh way of life to some extent.
But the grandsons who succeeded the Hindal 's sons,
Had gone completely astray from the Sikh way of life.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

These grandsons (who succeeded Hindal's sons), Declared themselves to be Niranjanias instead of Guru's Sikhs. Rather than following the Sikh way of worship in Gurdwaras, They induldged into acts of burglary in the Gurdwaras. (19)
lines: These grandsons (who succeeded Hindal's sons),
Declared themselves to be Niranjanias instead of Guru's Sikhs.
Rather than following the Sikh way of worship in Gurdwaras,
They induldged into acts of burglary in the Gurdwaras.

blocks.text: Several times had they stolen from Darbar Sahib (Amritsar), The expensive canopy from the ceiling of the sanctum sanctorum. Greeting each other with the words "Kartar, Kartar", They kept silent avoiding the reciting of "Waheguru". (20)
lines: Several times had they stolen from Darbar Sahib (Amritsar),
The expensive canopy from the ceiling of the sanctum sanctorum.
Greeting each other with the words "Kartar,
Kartar",
They kept silent avoiding the reciting of "Waheguru".

blocks.text: Sometime they professed to follow the religious order of Nanak, While at another moment they professed to be followers of Jinda Pir. Empathising and sympathesing with the Muslims, They shared their meals with the Sultanis as well. (21)
lines: Sometime they professed to follow the religious order of Nanak,
While at another moment they professed to be followers of Jinda Pir.
Empathising and sympathesing with the Muslims,
They shared their meals with the Sultanis as well.

blocks.text: The most wicked among them being one "Har Bhagat", Who was instrumental in getting many Sikhs eliminated. Being wicked, he conspired and spoke ill of (the Sikhs), As he had developed cordial relations with the Mughals. (22)
lines: The most wicked among them being one "Har Bhagat",
Who was instrumental in getting many Sikhs eliminated.
Being wicked, he conspired and spoke ill of (the Sikhs),
As he had developed cordial relations with the Mughals.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The Khalsa Panth had come into Being (among the masses), As a result of the teachings of the Sikh Gurus and their preaching. But if a Sikh approached them (considering them as Guru's Sikhs), He would catch hold of him and eliminate him. (23)
lines: The Khalsa Panth had come into Being (among the masses),
As a result of the teachings of the Sikh Gurus and their preaching.
But if a Sikh approached them (considering them as Guru's Sikhs),
He would catch hold of him and eliminate him.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

(Or else) he would handover the Sikhs to the Mughals at Lahore, And received the rewards in return for their arrest. Providing information, he would get the Sikhs arrested from their villages, As he kept a large battery of Mughal troops with him. (24)
lines: (Or else) he would handover the Sikhs to the Mughals at Lahore,
And received the rewards in return for their arrest.
Providing information, he would get the Sikhs arrested from their villages,
As he kept a large battery of Mughal troops with him.

blocks.text: Twice had he got my (the author's) own village ransacked, Which made my father and grandfather desert their home. Hindal was further succeeded by his great grandsons, Who were named Kirpal and Dyal respectively, (25)
lines: Twice had he got my (the author's) own village ransacked,
Which made my father and grandfather desert their home.
Hindal was further succeeded by his great grandsons,
Who were named Kirpal and Dyal respectively,

blocks.text: They led the troops of the (invading) Ahmed Shah, And got a large number of Sikhs eliminated through their guidance. They were responsible for the genocide of the Sikhs near Malerkotla, In which twenty to thirty thousand Sikhs lost their lives. (26)
lines: They led the troops of the (invading) Ahmed Shah,
And got a large number of Sikhs eliminated through their guidance.
They were responsible for the genocide of the Sikhs near Malerkotla,
In which twenty to thirty thousand Sikhs lost their lives.

blocks.text: When the Singhs launched an attack against them, Ahmed Shah (Abdali) had to rescue them from the Sikhs. After the Khalsa forces routed and packed Ahmed Shah Abdali, These two (wicked) Hindals patched up with the Sikhs. (27)
lines: When the Singhs launched an attack against them,
Ahmed Shah (Abdali) had to rescue them from the Sikhs.
After the Khalsa forces routed and packed Ahmed Shah Abdali,
These two (wicked) Hindals patched up with the Sikhs.

blocks.text: (But) Once during a factional fight among the Sikhs, Kirpal Hindal was killed while supporting one Sikh faction. (28)
lines: (But) Once during a factional fight among the Sikhs,
Kirpal Hindal was killed while supporting one Sikh faction.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Dyal Dass succeeded Kirpal (after the latter 's death), And occupied the seat of the (Jandialian Hindal). Sharan Dass happened to be the son of Dyal Dass, Who was extremely wicked and a dipsomaniac. (29)
lines: Dyal Dass succeeded Kirpal (after the latter 's death),
And occupied the seat of the (Jandialian Hindal).
Sharan Dass happened to be the son of Dyal Dass,
Who was extremely wicked and a dipsomaniac.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

He, being very muscular and tall in stature, Could consume one full-fledged goat's meat at a time. Being extremely lecherous and full of sexual lust, He would not spare anybody's daughter or daughter-in-law. (30)
lines: He, being very muscular and tall in stature,
Could consume one full-fledged goat's meat at a time.
Being extremely lecherous and full of sexual lust,
He would not spare anybody's daughter or daughter-in-law.

blocks.text: The Sikhs, being wary of his evil (sexual) designs, Felt reluctant to allow their daughters to attend his congregations. Then he concocted a tale (to cover up his evil designs), That one had to pay a very heavy price to become a Sikh. (31)
lines: The Sikhs, being wary of his evil (sexual) designs,
Felt reluctant to allow their daughters to attend his congregations.
Then he concocted a tale (to cover up his evil designs),
That one had to pay a very heavy price to become a Sikh.

blocks.text: That, as recorded in scriptures, to be a Sikh was more arduous, Than a walk over the razor's edge sharper than human hair. So manifestly great was the blessings of being a Sikh, That the offer of one's daughter or daughter-in-law was not a big deal. (32)
lines: That, as recorded in scriptures, to be a Sikh was more arduous,
Than a walk over the razor's edge sharper than human hair.
So manifestly great was the blessings of being a Sikh,
That the offer of one's daughter or daughter-in-law was not a big deal.

blocks.text: Since the daughters had been offered (to others) since eternity, There should no hesitation at all about this practice. Making such an interpolation into the Janaksakhi himself, He asked the congregation to see this (fact) for themselves. (33)
lines: Since the daughters had been offered (to others) since eternity,
There should no hesitation at all about this practice.
Making such an interpolation into the Janaksakhi himself,
He asked the congregation to see this (fact) for themselves.

blocks.text: Dohra:

This worthless progeny who received the Guru's blessings gratis, Perished without any achievement to their credit, They, being extremely wicked slanderers and sinners, Had no further family line (to carry on their dark deeds). (34)
lines: This worthless progeny who received the Guru's blessings gratis,
Perished without any achievement to their credit,
They, being extremely wicked slanderers and sinners,
Had no further family line (to carry on their dark deeds).
